title: Angada reassures the monkeys to return to the battle
introduction: Seeing Kumbhakarna coming with his colossal body and emitting a tremendous roar, the monkeys scare away. Angada reassures the monkeys, who then return to the battle field to resume fight. When the monkeys start attacking Kumbhakarna, the latter crushes some monkeys with rage. Then again, the monkeys get frightened and run away in different directions. Angada then restores the monkeys to confidence once more and all the monkeys stand awaiting the command of Angada.
closing: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे आदिकाव्ये युद्धकाण्डे षट्षष्टितमः सर्गः
Thus completes 66th Chapter of Yuddha Kanda of the glorious Ramayana of Valmiki, the work of a sage and the oldest epic.

verses.devanagari:
स लङ्घायित्वा प्राकारम् गिरिकूटोपमो महान् |
निर्ययौ निगरात्तूत्णम् कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः
verses.iast:
sa laṇ^ghāyitvā prākāram girikūṭopamo mahān |
niryayau nigarāttūtṇam kumbhakarṇo mahābalaḥ
verses.translation: That mighty Kumbhakarna, with his colossal body resembling the peak of a mountain, having crossed the rampart, sallied forth from the city.

glosses.meaning: resembling the peak of a mountain

verses.devanagari:
ननाद च महानादम् समुद्रमभिनादयन् |
विजयन्निव निर्घातान्विधमन्निव पर्वतान्
verses.iast:
nanāda ca mahānādam samudramabhinādayan |
vijayanniva nirghātānvidhamanniva parvatān
verses.translation: Kumbhakarna emitted a roar, making the sea to reverberate, causing the mountains to quake and drowning the thunder-claps, as it were.

verses.devanagari:
तमवध्यं मघवता यमेन वरुणेन च |
प्रेक्ष्य भीमाक्षमायान्तं वानरा विप्रदुद्रुवुः
verses.iast:
tamavadhyaṃ maghavatA yamena varuṇena ca |
prekṣya bhImAkṣamAyAntaṃ vAnarA vipradudruvuḥ
verses.translation: Seeing that demons of terrific eyes who could not be destroyed either by Indra the lord of celestials or by Yama the lord of death or by Varuna the god of water, the monkeys ran away.

glosses.meaning: or by Yama the lord of death
or by Varuna the lord of death

verses.devanagari:
तांस्तु विद्रवतो दृष्ट्वा वालिपुत्रोऽङ्गदोऽब्रवीत् |
नलं नीलं गवाक्षं च कुमुदं च महाबलम्
verses.iast:
tAṃstu vidravato dṛṣṭvA vAliputro'ñgado'bravIt |
nalaṃ nIlaṃ gavAkṣaṃ ca kumudaṃ ca mahAbalam
verses.translation: Seeing them running away, Angada the prince spoke to Nala, Neela, Gavaksha and the mighty Kumuda as follows:

verses.devanagari:
आत्मानमत्र विस्मृत्य वीर्याण्यभिजनानि च |
क्व गच्छत भयत्रस्ताः प्राकृता हरयो यथा
verses.iast:
AtmAnamatra vismṛtya vIryAṇyabhijanAni ca |
kva gacchata bhayatrastAḥ prAkṛtA harayo yathA
verses.translation: "Where do you go, forgetting your own dignities as also nobilities of birth and trembling with fear like common monkeys?"

glosses.meaning: and nobilities of bhaja trastaaH = and trembling with fear

verses.devanagari:
साधु सौम्या निवर्तध्वं किं प्राणान्परिरक्षथ |
नालं युद्धाय वै रक्षो महतीयं विभीषिकाः
verses.iast:
sAdhu saumyA nivartadhvaṃ kiṃ prAṇAnparirakṣatha |
nAlaṃ yuddhAya vai rakṣo mahatIyaṃ vibhIṣikAḥ
verses.translation: "O auspicious monkeys! Please return! Why do you so fully guard your lives? This demon is not competent for a combat. He is merely a great toy of terror."

verses.devanagari:
महतीमुत्थितामेनां राक्षसानां विभीषिकाम् |
विक्रमाद्विधमिष्यामो निवर्तध्वं प्लवङ्गमाः
verses.iast:
mahatImutthitAmenAṃ rAkṣasAnAṃ vibhIṣikAm |
vikramAdvidhamiṣyAmo nivartadhvaṃ plavañgamAḥ
verses.translation: "O monkeys! By our prowess, we shall destroy this giant toy produced by demons. Come back!"

verses.devanagari:
कृच्छ्रेण तु समाश्वास्य सङ्गम्य च ततस्ततः |
वृक्षाद्रिहस्ता हरयः सम्प्रतस्थू रणाजिरम्
verses.iast:
kṛcchreṇa tu samAśvAsya sañgamya ca tatastataḥ |
vṛkṣAdrihastA harayaḥ sampratasthU raṇAjiram
verses.translation: Reconciling themselves with some difficulty, the monkeys, from all sides, assembled together at a place and snatching some trees, the monkeys for their part, towards the battle-field.

verses.devanagari:
ते निवृत्य तु सङ्क्रुद्धाः कुम्भकर्णं वनौकसः |
निजघ्नुः परमक्रुद्धाः समदा इव कुञ्जराः
verses.iast:
te nivṛtya tu sañkruddhAḥ kumbhakarṇaṃ vanaukasaḥ |
nijaghnuḥ paramakruddhAḥ samadA iva kuñjarAḥ
verses.translation: Like elephants in rut, those monkeys, having came back, hurriedly hit Kumbhakarna, very much enraged as they were.

glosses.meaning: kuNjaraaH iva = like elephants in rut

verses.devanagari:
प्रांशुभिर्गिरिशृङ्गैश्च शिलाभिश्च महाबलाः |
पादपैः पुष्पिताग्रैश्च हन्यमानो न कम्पते
verses.iast:
prAṃśubhirgiriśṛñgaiśca śilAbhiśca mahAbalAḥ |
pAdapaiḥ puṣpitAgraiśca hanyamAno na kampate
verses.translation: The mighty Kumbhakarna, though assaulted with lofty mountain-tops, rocks and trees with blossoms at their ends, stood unshaken.

glosses.meaning: and trees having blossoms at their ends

verses.devanagari:
तस्य गात्रेषु पतिता भिद्यन्ते शतशः शिलाः |
पादपाः पुष्पिताग्राश्च भग्नाः पेतुर्महीतले
verses.iast:
tasya gAtreṣu patitA bhidyante śataśaḥ śilAḥ |
pAdapAḥ puṣpitAgrAśca bhagnAḥ peturmahItale
verses.translation: Many rocks, fallen on his limbs, got burst into pieces. The trees, with blossoms at their ends, were broken and fell shattered on the floor.

verses.devanagari:
सोऽपि सैन्यानि सङ्क्रुद्धो वानराणां महौजसाम् |
ममन्थ परमायत्तो वनान्यग्निरिवोत्थितः
verses.iast:
so'pi sainyAni sañkruddho vAnarAṇAṃ mahaujasAm |
mamantha paramAyatto vanAnyagnirivotthitaḥ
verses.translation: Kumbhakarna too, very much enraged, crushed the ranks of monkeys though they were greatly energetic, with his extreme exertion even as a rising fire would consume the woods.

glosses.meaning: of the ranks of monkeys though there were greatly energetic
with his extreme exertion utthitaH agniH vanaaniiva = even as a rising fire would consume the woods.

verses.devanagari:
लोहितार्द्रास्तु बहवः शेरते वानरर्षभाः |
निरस्ताः पतिता भूमौ ताम्रपुष्पा इव द्रुमाः
verses.iast:
lohitArdrAstu bahavaḥ śerate vAnararṣabhAḥ |
nirastAḥ patitA bhUmau tAmrapuṣpA iva drumAḥ
verses.translation: Many of the foremost among the monkeys lay on the ground, bathed in blood as they were, fallen like trees with crimson flowers, when tossed up by the demon.

glosses.meaning: of the foremost among the monkeys

verses.devanagari:
लङ्घयन्तः प्रधावन्तो वानरा नावलोकयन् |
के चित्समुद्रे पतिताः के चिद्गगनमाश्रिताः
verses.iast:
lañghayantaḥ pradhAvanto vAnarA nAvalokayan |
ke citsamudre patitAḥ ke cidgaganamAśritAḥ
verses.translation: Some monkeys, while jumping and running away, did not look back. Some fell in the ocean. Some inhabited the sky.

verses.devanagari:
वध्यमानास्तु ते वीरा राक्षसेन बलीयसा |
सागरं येन ते तीर्णाः पथा तेनैव दुद्रुवुः
verses.iast:
vadhyamAnAstu te vIrA rAkṣasena balIyasA |
sAgaraṃ yena te tIrṇAḥ pathA tenaiva dudruvuḥ
verses.translation: While that demon was killing some warriors of monkeys playfully, some others ran away by the same route, by which they earlier crossed the ocean.

verses.devanagari:
ते स्थलानि तथा निम्नं विषण्णवदना भयात् |
ऋक्षा वृक्षान्समारूढाः के चित्पर्वतमाश्रिताः
verses.iast:
te sthalAni tathA nimnaṃ viṣaṇṇavadanA bhayAt |
ṛkṣA vṛkṣAnsamArUḍhAḥ ke citparvatamAśritAḥ
verses.translation: While some monkeys becoming pale-faced due to fear, inhabited the mounds and the low grounds, some bears ascended the trees. Some escaped to a hill.

verses.devanagari:
ममज्जुरर्णवे के चिद्गुहाः के चित्समाश्रिताः |
निषेदुः प्लवगाः के चित्के चिन्नैवावतस्थिरे
केचिद्भूमौ निपतिताः केचित्सुप्ता मृता इव |
verses.iast:
mamajjurarṇave ke cidguhAḥ ke citsamAśritAḥ |
niṣeduḥ plavagAḥ ke citke cinnaivAvatasthire
kecidbhūmau nipatitāḥ kecitsuptā mṛtā iva |
verses.translation: Some were drowned in the ocean. Some had recourse into the caves. Some others escaped. Some could not even stand stable on the ground. Some fell down. Some lied down, as though they were dead.

verses.devanagari:
तान्समीक्ष्याङ्गदो भङ्गान्वानरानिदमब्रवीत्
अवतिष्ठत युध्यामो निवर्तध्वं प्लवङ्गमाः |
verses.iast:
tAnsamIkṣyAñgado bhañgAnvAnarAnidamabravIt
avatiṣṭhata yudhyAmo nivartadhvaṃ plavañgamAḥ |
verses.translation: Seeing those monkeys disorderly retreated, Angada spoke these words, "Stay. We shall carry on the battle. Come back."

glosses.meaning: we shall carry on the battle

verses.devanagari:
भग्नानां वो न पश्यामि परिगम्य महीमिमाम्
स्थानं सर्वे निवर्तध्वं किं प्राणान्परिरक्षथ |
verses.iast:
bhagnAnAṃ vo na paśyAmi parigamya mahImimAm
sthAnaṃ sarve nivartadhvaṃ kiṃ prAṇAnparirakṣatha |
verses.translation: "I do not catch sight of any place for you, who have retreated, even if you roam over the entire earth. Let all of you come back. Why do you safeguard your lives?"

glosses.meaning: I do not catch sight of
(even if) you roam iverl unaan naguun = this earth

verses.devanagari:
निरायुधानां द्रवतामसङ्गगतिपौरुषाः
दारा ह्यपहसिष्यन्ति स वै घातस्तु जीविताम् |
verses.iast:
nirAyudhAnAṃ dravatAmasañgagatipauruṣAḥ
dArA hyapahasiṣyanti sa vai ghAtastu jIvitAm |
verses.translation: "O valiant monkeys, moving without hindrances! Your wives, seeing you running away leaving your weapos aside, will mock at you. It is indeed a death for those who lived well."

verses.devanagari:
कुलेषु जाताः सर्वे स्म विस्तीर्णेषु महत्सु च
क्व गच्छत भयत्रस्ताः प्राकृता हरयो यथा |
अनार्याः खलु यद्भीतास्त्यक्त्वा वीर्यं प्रधावत
verses.iast:
kuleṣu jAtAḥ sarve sma vistIrṇeṣu mahatsu ca
kva gacchata bhayatrastāḥ prākṛtā harayo yathā |
anAryAḥ khalu yadbhItAstyaktvA vIryaṃ pradhAvata
verses.translation: "All of us are born in distinguished races; which are well developed. Where to you go frightened, like ordinary monkeys? As you are running away with fear, leaving all your valour, you are indeed unworthy of honour."

glosses.meaning: you are indeed not worthy of honour.

verses.devanagari:
विकत्थनानि वो यानि यदा वै जनसंसदि |
तानि वः क्व च यतानि सोदग्राणि महान्ति च
verses.iast:
vikatthanAni vo yAni yadA vai janasaṃsadi |
tAni vaḥ kva ca yatAni sodagrAṇi mahAnti ca
verses.translation: "Where did those boasting words of you melt away, in which you highly projected yourself in front of the people just before coming for the battle?

glosses.meaning: at that time (before coming for the battle)?

verses.devanagari:
भीरुप्रवादाः श्रूयन्ते यस्तु जीवति धिक्कृतः |
मार्गः सत्पुरुषैर्जुष्टः सेव्यतां त्यज्यतां भयम्
verses.iast:
bhIrupravAdAḥ śrUyante yastu jIvati dhikkṛtaḥ |
mArgaḥ satpuruṣairjuṣṭaḥ sevyatAṃ tyajyatAṃ bhayam
verses.translation: "The cowards, who survive even after being reproached, have to hear slanders from the people. Let the path trodden by the good people be followed. Let your fear be abandoned."

verses.devanagari:
शयामहे वा निहताः पृथिव्यामल्पजीविताः |
प्राप्नुयामो ब्रह्मलोकम् दुष्प्रपम् च कुयोधिभिः
verses.iast:
śayAmahe vA nihatAḥ pṛthivyAmalpajIvitAḥ |
prāpnuyāmo brahmalokam duṣprapam ca kuyodhibhiḥ
verses.translation: "If our longevity is short, we shall lie down, being killed by the enemies, on the earth and reach the realm of Brahma (residence of pious spirits), which is difficult to be attained by bad warriors."

glosses.meaning: the realm of Brahma (residence of pious spirits)

verses.devanagari:
अवाप्नुयामः कीर्तिम् वा निहत्वा शत्रुमाहवे |
निहता वीरलोकस्य भोक्ष्यामो वसु वानराः
verses.iast:
avāpnuyāmaḥ kīrtim vā nihatvā śatrumāhave |
nihatā vīralokasya bhokṣyāmo vasu vānarāḥ
verses.translation: "O monkeys! We shall obtain glory by killing our enemies in battle or if killed on the other hand, we shall enjoy the heaven, attained by the warriors."

glosses.meaning: of the world attained by warriors.

verses.devanagari:
न कुम्भकर्णः काकुत्स्थं दृष्ट्वा जीवन्गमिष्यति |
दीप्यमानमिवासाद्य पतङ्गो ज्वलनं यथा
verses.iast:
na kumbhakarṇaḥ kAkutsthaṃ dṛṣṭvA jIvangamiṣyati |
dIpyamAnamivAsAdya patañgo jvalanaṃ yathA
verses.translation: "Coming face to face with Rama, Kumbhakarna will not go back alive, any more than a moth meeting a blazing fire."

verses.devanagari:
पलायनेन चोद्दिष्टाः प्राणान्रक्षामहे वयम् |
एकेन बहवो भग्ना यशो नाशं गमिष्यति
verses.iast:
palAyanena coddiṣṭAḥ prAṇAnrakṣAmahe vayam |
ekena bahavo bhagnA yaśo nAśaṃ gamiṣyati
verses.translation: "If we, in large numbers, who are intended to fight, are conquered by one person alone and if we protect our lives by running away, our glory will undergo a damage."

verses.devanagari:
एवं ब्रुवाणं तं शूरमङ्गदं कनकाङ्गदम् |
द्रवमाणास्ततो वाक्यमूचुः शूरविगर्हितम्
verses.iast:
evaṃ bruvAṇaṃ taṃ śUramañgadaṃ kanakAñgadam |
dravamAṇAstato vAkyamUcuḥ śUravigarhitam
verses.translation: Then, those fleeing monkeys spoke the following words, which were contemptible by the warriors, to that valiant Angada, who was adorneed with golden armlets.

glosses.meaning: who was adorned with golden armlets

verses.devanagari:
कृतं नः कदनं घोरं कुम्भकर्णेन रक्षसा |
न स्थानकालो गच्छामो दयितं जीवितं हि नः
verses.iast:
kṛtaṃ naḥ kadanaṃ ghoraṃ kumbhakarṇena rakṣasA |
na sthAnakAlo gacchAmo dayitaṃ jIvitaṃ hi naḥ
verses.translation: "For us, it is enough of this terrific battle with Kumbhakarna, the demon. It is not the proper time to stay back but it is to time to go away. Life is indeed dear to us."

glosses.meaning: it is not the proper time to stay

verses.devanagari:
एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं सर्वे ते भेजिरे दिशः |
भीमं भीमाक्षमायान्तं दृष्ट्वा वानरयूथपाः
verses.iast:
etAvaduktvA vacanaṃ sarve te bhejire diśaḥ |
bhImaṃ bhImAkṣamAyAntaṃ dṛṣṭvA vAnarayUthapAḥ
verses.translation: Seeing that terrific Kumbhakarna coming with his dreadful eyes, all those commanders of monkey-troops, speaking words only thus far, scattered in all directions.

verses.devanagari:
द्रवमाणास्तु ते वीरा अङ्गदेन वलीमुखाः |
सान्त्वैश्च बहुमानैश्च ततः सर्वे निवर्तिताः
verses.iast:
dravamAṇAstu te vIrA añgadena valImukhAḥ |
sAntvaiśca bahumAnaiśca tataḥ sarve nivartitAḥ
verses.translation: Thereafter, with the coaxing words and inferential arguments by Angada, all those fleeing commanders of monkeys turned back.

verses.devanagari:
प्रहर्षमुपनीताश्च वालिपुत्रेण धीमता |
आज्ञाप्रतीक्षास्तुस्थुश्च सर्वे वानरयूथपाः
verses.iast:
praharṣamupanītāśca vāliputreṇa dhīmatā |
ājJṇāpratīkṣāstusthuśca sarve vānarayūthapāḥ
verses.translation: Having been cheered up by the intellectual Angada, all those commanders of the army-troops stood awaiting his command.

verses.devanagari:
ऋषभशरभमैन्दधूम्रनीलाः |
कुमुदसुषेणगवाक्षरम्भताराः|
द्विविदपनसवायुपुत्रमुख्यास् |
त्वरिततराभिमुखं रणं प्रयाताः
verses.iast:
ṛṣabhaśarabhamaindadhUmranIlAḥ |
kumudasuṣeṇagavAkṣarambhatArAḥ |
dvividapanasavAyuputramukhyAs |
tvaritatarAbhimukhaṃ raṇaṃ prayAtAḥ
verses.translation: Rishabha, Sharabha, Mainda, Dhumra, Neela, Kumuda, sushena, Gavaksha, Rambha, Tara and more particularly Dvipada, Panasa and hanuma marched ahead very quickly, with their faces turned towards the battle.

glosses.meaning: very quickly with their faces turned towards
